title: The Sleepy Outskirts
story: Leaving Los Cipreses Waypost behind at sunrise, James followed the winding dirt path as it gently dropped into the valley floor. The crisp highland air gradually warmed, smelling of dry pine needles and woodsmoke. For hours, he walked with steady purpose, his brass map canister tapping against his hip in time with his steps. By mid-afternoon, the wide open valley gave way to the quiet outskirts of a forgotten settlement. James had never seen buildings so worn by time and weather. He had never seen walls where green moss climbed so freely through the cracks of adobe bricks. He had never seen streets where tall grass grew quietly between the uneven cobblestones. Unlike the bustling, polished avenues of Oakhaven, this place felt soft, slow, and half-asleep under the warm sun. He passed a rustic wooden gate hanging from a single iron hinge and paused near an overgrown orchard. Peering through his green sea-glass, the cracked clay tiles and faded red rooflines took on an emerald shimmer. A rusty iron pump near a stone trough dripped rhythmically onto a smooth grey stone, a slow dripping sound that briefly reminded him of the quiet water-clocks in Barnaby's workshop. As evening drew near, James reached the edge of a modest, sleepy village anchored by a weather-beaten stone archway. A cracked wooden sign nearby bore faded lettering that read Aldea San Gabriel. He climbed onto a low stone wall under the shade of a flowering jacaranda tree, unstrapping his leather belt to settle his treasures beside him. Below, a single wisp of smoke drifted from a crooked tin chimney, while the setting sun painted the ancient crumbling walls in soft shades of gold.
